original_question: Which Atlastin gene is associated with Strumpell-Lorrain disease, an inherited condition characterized by progressively increasing spasticity in the lower limbs?

final_qi.question: Which Atlastin gene is associated with Strumpell-Lorrain disease, an inherited condition characterized by progressively increasing spasticity in the lower limbs?
final_qi.long_answer: Mutations in the ATL1 gene, which encodes the dynamin-like GTPase atlastin-1, cause the SPG3A form of hereditary spastic paraplegia (Strumpell-Lorrain disease). Altered ATL1 disrupts endoplasmic-reticulum network dynamics in corticospinal motor neurons, leading to the characteristic progressive spasticity of the lower limbs.

0.question: Which Atlastin gene is associated with Strumpell-Lorrain disease?

final_answer.long_answer: Strumpell-Lorrain disease—also called autosomal-dominant hereditary spastic paraplegia type 3A—is most commonly caused by mutations in the ATL1 gene, which encodes the dynamin-like GTPase Atlastin-1. Defects in ATL1 impair endoplasmic-reticulum membrane fusion in long corticospinal neurons, leading to the progressive lower-limb spasticity characteristic of the disorder.
